newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish firms seek cut in social security payments.
newsitem.headline: Polish firms seek cut in social security payments.

text.p: Small- and mid-sized Polish firms would honestly pay insurance premiums to the state social security agency if they did not exceed 25 percent of gross wages, a survey by the National Chamber of Commerce (KIG) said.

The survey of 120 businesses in the western Wielkopolska region and Pomorze region near the Baltic Sea showed 66 percent of firms avoid such payments by employing people unofficially or officially paying higher wages than declared.
As a result, the state social security agency, ZUS, loses 30 to 40 percent of its dues from small- and mid-sized firms.

KIG said it would be possible to decrease insurance premiums by 15 to 20 percent from the current 48 percent if the so-called "grey zone" of unregistered and untaxed employment was decreased and if ZUS debtors among large firms, currently enjoying a moratorium, paid up.
